correctness.rationale: For any independent finite-second-moment preparation the area martingale terms have zero expectation on bounded time intervals. With the stated doubled convention the rate is p^T(AM_t−M_tA)q and M_t=A^(−1)+exp(−At)(M_0−A^(−1))exp(−At). The stationary term cancels, and combining eigenbasis entries yields exactly one candidate exponential per unordered pair. Coalescing equal exponents and removing zero coefficients can only reduce the count. A nonzero sum of s distinct real exponentials has at most s−1 real zeros with multiplicities by multiplication by one exponential and Rolle induction. Dyadic drift eigenvalues yield m=binom(d,2) distinct pair sums, and the given orthonormal plane coordinates have all pair minors nonzero. The (m−1)-by-m interpolation matrix has full row rank by the same zero lemma. A nonzero kernel combination then has exactly the prescribed zeros, each simple; for d=2 this just selects a nonzero single exponential and the empty set. Every coefficient is independently tunable by a symmetric off-diagonal covariance perturbation, which remains strictly positive definite after sufficiently small scaling. Rotations give the construction in any chosen plane. Sharpness permits choosing the drift, not promising saturation for each preassigned drift.
residual_risks: The all-dimension and arbitrary-time statements are analytic, not established by finite interpolation tests. No formal verification or expert attestation.

value.rationale: The exact dimension-dependent ceiling and the arbitrary-time realization distinguish transient covariance dynamics from stationary breaking of detailed balance. They show that even arbitrarily near equilibrium a reversible diffusion can exhibit a maximally complicated signed-area transient, and specify exactly how many such reversals fit in a given dimension.
